demonstrated_gap: The layer has never compared Claude Code's first-party LSP tool (shipped since v2.0.74; still being fixed as of v2.1.280, Sept 2026). The 2026-09-22 adjudication weighed only Serena, codebase-memory-mcp and jCodeMunch, and a repository grep finds no evaluation of the native tool. Serena's win on the Claude side therefore rests on a comparison set that left out the native path. The native tool offers the same language-server operations Serena wraps: definition, references, implementations, call hierarchy, and file and workspace symbols. It needs no MCP server and no permission prompt. It also pushes server diagnostics automatically after every Edit or Write, where Serena returns diagnostics only when get_diagnostics_for_file is called explicitly. Anthropic maintains the plugins in its official marketplace, which auto-updates by default: pyright-lsp uses pyright-langserver and typescript-lsp uses typescript-language-server. Recent fixes bear directly on our worker and token practice. Background subagents can use the tool (2.1.280). A language-server reconnect no longer invalidates the whole prompt cache (2.1.235). findReferences skips gitignored files (2.1.47). Limits: it returns locations, not symbol bodies, so exact source needs a native Read with a line range, and it serves Claude only. Codex has no native LSP client (openai/codex #8745 and #8633 are open), so Serena would stay as Codex's path.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Rerun the sealed eight-check set from foundation-native-20260920 (Python and CJS symbol, source and reference checks), plus added cross-file TS/JS reference questions. Use fresh Claude Code sessions on linux-wsl2-x86_64 and macos-arm64, with pyright-lsp and typescript-lsp at local scope and Serena disabled, then the same run with Serena enabled. Keep the Python backend fixed (pyright). Native path wins if LSP plus Read line-range returns at least Serena's correct definitions and references (precision and recall against the sealed answers) and the exact source text. It must also cost no more total tool-output and session tokens (exact o200k compare plus the ccusage session total), cause no prompt-cache invalidation, and have acceptable cold start and language-server memory. If so, the Claude lane moves to the native LSP and Serena stays for Codex. A missed reference, or higher total cost from extra Read calls, keeps Serena as the Claude default.

demonstrated_gap: Codex has no native LSP client (openai/codex #8745 and #8633 open). Its only language-server path is Serena, a Python app pinned to an unreleased dev commit that has been GPL-3.0-or-later since 2026-09-14. mcpls is a single Apache-2.0 Rust binary with checksummed releases for linux x86_64 and macOS Apple Silicon. It exposes the same LSP operations to any MCP client, Codex included: get_definition, get_references, go_to_implementation, get_incoming_calls and get_outgoing_calls, workspace_symbol_search, get_diagnostics and rename_symbol. Python defaults to pyright, with ty as an option. It cannot fetch a symbol body by name path the way Serena's find_symbol include_body does. Its maturity is thin: 73 stars, created 2025-12-24, and one human maintainer with 167 commits (the next has 7). It is a comparison arm, not a replacement now.

Also compare tool-schema plus tool-output tokens (exact o200k), install from the checksummed release, and language-server lifecycle cleanliness across three client restarts (no orphaned servers). mcpls becomes a targeted candidate or Codex co-default only if it matches Serena's correctness at lower tokens and setup cost.

demonstrated_gap: This targets the layer's open gap between its two current lanes. Serena gives compiler-grade references but keeps no persistent index, so it pays language-server warm-up each session. codebase-memory-mcp and the other tree-sitter graphs keep an index but resolve references heuristically. gortex keeps a persistent on-disk SQLite graph, updated by an fsnotify daemon. It can optionally confirm references through real language servers: pyright for Python, and tsgo or typescript-language-server for TS/JS. It ships as a single static binary for macOS and Linux under Apache-2.0 and supports both Claude Code and Codex CLI. Evidence is weak so far. Its benchmark is self-authored and its baseline is ripgrep verbatim matching (recall@2k 1.00 vs 0.00 on identifier queries), with no LSP or Serena baseline. It exposes 175 MCP tools (configurable), churns heavily (2,707 default-branch commits since 2026-06-27; still v0.x) and has one dominant maintainer (4,009 commits against 303 for the next). Compare it; do not adopt it yet.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Use a sealed task set on this repo covering Python and CJS definitions and references, multi-hop questions (callers of callers, affected tests), and a rename or delete followed by a re-query, which addresses the open symbol update and deletion correctness gap. Run gortex with pyright/tsgo resolution enabled and a restricted tool tier. Compare against Serena (references) and codebase-memory-mcp (multi-hop). Count correct answers, cold index time, fsnotify update latency and correctness after the edit, daemon RSS, and tool-schema plus output tokens. It moves to targeted candidate only if it matches Serena's reference correctness and beats codebase-memory-mcp on multi-hop at comparable total indexing and maintenance cost.

Offers 175 configurable MCP tools and a long-running daemon with fsnotify and an on-disk SQLite graph. Ships a single static binary for macOS, Linux and Windows. demonstrated_gap: The requirement is exact source and references 'for changes'. Serena answers one-hop references per symbol. Asking which callers, dependents and tests a diff affects takes chained find_referencing_symbols calls plus reads, and no current winner answers it in one call. code-review-graph keeps an incremental tree-sitter graph: it re-parses only files whose SHA-256 changed, which it reports at about 2.5 s after a two-file edit on a ~3,000-file repo (about 40 s cold). It returns a diff's blast radius and ships installers for Codex and Claude Code. Its own FAQ concedes LSP is more precise per symbol and grep wins one-hop lookups. Its published accuracy is impact F1 0.69 scored against graph-derived ground truth, whose recall is circular, so no independent accuracy evidence exists yet. The head is unchanged since the star audit (6b12d116).
comparison_that_would_overturn: Take N sealed diffs from this repo's history. Ground truth is the files the author actually co-changed plus the tests that fail when the change is reverted. Compare predicted affected files and tests (precision and recall) and total tokens for three arms: code-review-graph, Serena reference chains plus known-source reads, and codebase-memory-mcp trace_path. Include measured cold build and incremental update cost on both hosts. It would earn a complementary change-impact lane only if it beats both on recall at comparable precision and cost.
